newsitem.title: TAIWAN: China Steel in $1.6 bln Australia deal.
newsitem.headline: China Steel in $1.6 bln Australia deal.

text.p: China Steel Corp, Taiwan's largest steel maker, said on Tuesday it has signed 10-year contracts with two Australian firms to buy US$1.6 billion worth of iron ore form them.
The two firms are Broken Hill Proprietary Company Ltd and Hamersley Iron Proprietary Ltd, a China Steel spokesman told Reuters.
"We just formally signed 10-year, US$1.6 billion contracts with Broken Hill and Hamersley to buy iron ore from them for our fourth steel plant," the spokesman said.
China Steel's fourth plant, with a designed capacity of 2.4 million tonnes of steel, was expected to start operations by the end of 1996, he said.
"(After) Adding the new plant, our annual production capacity should reach 8.05 million tonnes of crude steel in 1997 from the current 5.65 million," he said.
China Steel, previously state-owned, was privatised in April 1995.
